newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolian oil product prices up 5.4 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian oil product prices up 5.4 pct in Dec.

text.p: Prices of oil products in Mongolia climbed an average 5.4 percent in December, the Government News newspaper said on Friday.

The price of 76 octane petrol was 212 tugriks ($0.30) per litre as of January 1, up from 200 tugriks on December 3, the newspaper quoted an official of the state-run oil importer and distributor Neft Import Concern as saying.

The price of 93 octane petrol had risen to 247 tugriks from 235 tugriks during the period while diesel was selling for 249 tugriks a litre, up from 237 tugriks, it quoted Neft deputy director G. Manibadar, as saying.
Increases in international oil prices had caused the rises, Manibadar said without elaborating.
Mongolia, which imports all of its oil, mostly from Russia, freed energy prices last September to bring domestic prices in line with world levels.
Fuel prices rocketed 43-80 percent from September to December. Neft officials said those increases were due largely to the weakness of the tugrik.
